newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in pre-PPI shuffle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in pre-PPI shuffle.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities narrowed modestly to Treasuries in light trading on Tuesday, analysts said.
Investors' squaring of their portfolios and looking ahead to the week's inflation data held prices lower, analysts said.
A strong BTM/Schroders chain store sales report -- showing a 1.0 percent increase in sales during the first week of December -- set a somewhat depressed tone for the session, they said.
Pass-throughs generally fell about 1/32 to 7/32 overall by late Tuesday afternoon.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 4/32 at 100-31/32, yielding 116 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Fannie Mae 7.5s were off 4/32 at 100-26/32, and Freddie Mac 7.5s were off 4/32 at 100-30/32.
The 10-year note yield had risen to 6.22 percent, with the note's price falling 8/32.

The week's first major data, the Producer Price Index for November, will be released on Wednesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. A consensus appears to have built for a 0.3 percent overall gain, with a 0.2 percent increase in core components.
